Laps without a start time are placed at race start, which gives false timings.
No tests are visible in the packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Source notes and imports
sections.what: The header says the source is unofficial and prototype only, and that laps with no time stay blank. It brings in the checking library and shared types.
sections.why: The warning stops anyone mistaking this prototype data for licensed data.
sections.watch_out: The source's rights policy must still allow use, or the rights check will block it.

sections.name: session
sections.title: Shape of a race session record
sections.what: Describes the session fields kept from the feed: key, name, start date, year, country, location and circuit. Extra fields are allowed.
sections.why: Keeps every session checked before the race is built.
sections.watch_out: If the start date format changes, every race start time breaks.

sections.name: lap, OpenF1Doc
sections.title: Shape of lap records and the input bundle
sections.what: Describes one lap by driver and lap number, with optional start time, duration and pit-out flag. It also defines the bundle that holds the sessions, the laps and the key of the race to build.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps raw feed data consistent before it is used.
sections.watch_out: Laps may have empty times, so any new code must handle them rather than assume a value.

sections.name: parseOpenF1
sections.title: Building a race from laps
sections.what: Finds the requested race in the sessions list, keeps its laps, and puts them in the order each lap ended. It records each lap with its time since the race start, lists the cars, and leaves the result blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: the feed has no result, so the code orders laps by time rather than guessing a winner.
sections.watch_out: Laps with no start time are placed at the race start, so their timestamps are wrong.

summary: Turns one OpenF1 race session of lap timing records into a race with one incident per lap.
purpose: It lets the app show Formula 1 race laps in order, for a prototype only.
why: The lap feed is the only timing data available, so the app shows laps rather than a result it cannot verify.
how: It checks the session list and the laps. It finds the session with the requested key, keeps only that session's laps, works out when each lap ended, sorts them, and creates one lap record for each. It also lists the cars that appear and returns an empty outcome.
inputs: A bundle containing the sessions list, the laps list, and the session key to parse.
outputs: A ParsedEvent with one lap incident per lap, the list of cars, and no result.
risks: This source is unofficial. Laps without a start time are placed at the race start, so their order and time are wrong.
debug: If a session is not found, the error says which session key was missing from the sessions list. If lap times look wrong, check whether the lap has a start time and a duration. Check the prototype flag in the source's rights policy.
